newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian separatists kill six soldiers in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Indian separatists kill six soldiers in ambush.

text.p: Separatist guerrillas in the northeast Indian state of Assam blew up an army vehicle with a remote-controlled bomb on Wednesday, killing six soldiers, police said.
They said the guerrillas used a crudely-assembled bomb in the incident that took place at Tangla in Darrang district, some 70 km (45 miles) north of the state's main city, Guwahati.
Separatist guerrillas of the United Liberation Front of Asom (ULFA) have been fighting for an independent state since 1979 in the tea and oil rich state.
They accuse New Delhi's federal government of exploiting Assam's rich mineral and forest resources while ignoring regional development.
Security forces have launched a manhunt for the guerrillas responsible for Wednesday's incident, officials said.
